name: Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Laboratory
notes: The Daya Bay official experiment site (dayabay.ihep.ac.cn) timed out on every fetch attempt; this record relies on the INSPIRE experiment record, the 2012 discovery paper (arXiv:1203.1669), the detector paper (arXiv:1309.1557), and Wikipedia (used only for the pointer-level facts noted per field).

This facility record covers the three underground experimental halls (Daya Bay near, Ling Ao near, far hall) as one reactor-neutrino site complex; no source consulted gives distinct, separately sourced coordinates for the individual halls (see the note on site:daya-bay-experimental-halls).

operator.note: IHEP leads the Daya Bay collaboration per general knowledge of the experiment's structure, but no page consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states an explicit 'operator' of the underground halls themselves (as distinct from the collaboration); recorded as uncertain rather than asserted as verified.
operator.value: Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), Chinese Academy of Sciences

summary.plain: A set of underground experimental halls near the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power plants in Guangdong, China, built to catch antineutrinos streaming out of the reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site hosting three underground experimental halls (two near halls and one far hall) at baselines of 470 m, 576 m and 1648 m from six 2.9 GW_th reactor cores at the Daya Bay and Ling Ao nuclear power complexes, Guangdong, China.
